open_obligations: Check that the correlation in Figure 3-right holds on held-out questions (the authors use separate cross-play and self-play sets)
Note that the authors themselves call this 'weak evidence' and that debaters are far from optimal play
out.other_title: AI safety via debate: zero-sum self-play debate game judged by a human
out.rationale: The authors explicitly frame their Elo-accuracy trend as weak evidence for Irving et al.'s claim that debate at optimal play yields truth; the support is directional, as debaters are far from optimal and only inference-time optimised.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Whether stronger debate play yields more truthful judge outcomes; holds for inference-time optimisation, not trained debaters

text: The authors report a strong correlation between debaters' aggregate Elo and self-play judge accuracy, so optimising debaters for judge preference improves accuracy. They say this provides weak evidence that under optimal play debate produces truthful information (Irving et al., 2018).
title: Khan et al. find judge accuracy rises with debater Elo, weak evidence for Irving et al.'s optimal-play claim
